transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Gotcha, thanks for sharing that — those after-hours intake calls going to voicemail are exactly where we help.  

When those calls hit voicemail right now, do people usually leave a message, or do they just hang up and call the next place?
User: Most don't leave a message. They hang up and likely call the next place.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly where a lot of money quietly walks out the door.  

So roughly how many of those after-hours calls would you say hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go straight to voicemail.
Agent: Got it, 12 a week is a lot of people you never really get to talk to.  

What kind of business are you running, just so I can picture what those callers are usually looking for?
User: We're a personal injury law firm. Callers usually seek legal representation for accidents or injuries.
Agent: That helps a lot, thanks — for PI, even one of those 12 missed calls could be a big case.  

Are you mainly losing these during weekday evenings, or is it more nights and weekends?
User: It's mainly during nights and weekends when our office is closed.
Agent: Right, that lines up — a big chunk of accident calls come in exactly then.  

Are you looking for a way to actually answer and qualify those night/weekend calls so you’re not losing cases, or are you more just exploring what’s possible right now?
User: We're definitely looking for a way to answer and qualify those calls to avoid losing potential cases.
Agent: Makes total sense, especially in PI where one good case more than pays for fixing this.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those 12 missed calls a week might actually be costing you in lost fee revenue?
User: Not yet, but we estimate about 70% of those would book if someone answered, averaging $1,800 per intake.
Agent: Makes sense, and your math’s pretty close — on those numbers you’re leaking around sixty-five grand a month in cases just from after-hours voicemail.  

So… let’s walk you through how to plug that; it’s a quick 20‑minute rundown where we map this to your firm — is later today or sometime tomorrow better for you?
User: Sometime tomorrow would be better for me.
Agent: Perfect, we can do tomorrow.  

First thing — what’s your first name?
User: I'm Marcus.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Marcus.  

And your last name?
Agent: Got it, Marcus.  

And what’s your last name, spelled slowly for me?
User: It's Bell, with Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Thanks, Marcus Bell at Bell & Associates Legal — perfect.  

And the number you’re calling from now, ending in 0001, is that the best number to reach you for the follow-up?
Agent: Got it, we’ll use that one.  

And Marcus, which time zone are you in — Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Yes, +19172120001 is the best number to reach me for the follow-up.
Agent: Mhm, perfect, thanks for confirming.  

So the earliest I can get you in is Wednesday at 3:30 or 4:15 in the afternoon Eastern — which works better for you?
User: Wednesday at 3:30 Eastern works for me. Yes, book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks, Marcus — you’re all set for Wednesday at 3:30 Eastern with Jay. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation and a link in case you ever need to reschedule.

Is there anything else you need from me right now?

Alright, really glad you called in today. Jay’s looking forward to meeting you and walking through how to stop those after-hours cases from slipping away. Have a great rest of your day — bye!
